conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee, one of your surgical team doctors. You’re here because of a nonhealing wound on your right foot after your toe amputation. We need to check the blood flow there with an angiogram. How are you feeling tonight?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’m okay, just a little tired. The foot’s not hurting much, but it’s been slow to heal. Is that why I’m here again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Because of your diabetes and circulation issues, wounds can take longer to heal. We want to make sure there’s enough blood flow to the area. That’s what the angiogram will show.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Is it a surgery? Will I be out long?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a minimally invasive procedure. We’ll insert a small catheter in your groin and take images of the arteries in your leg. You’ll be awake but sedated. It usually takes about an hour.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I had dialysis today already, right? I saw the team earlier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you had your scheduled hemodialysis this morning. That helps us manage your fluids and potassium before the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. My potassium’s been tricky before. Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re watching it closely. Your level was 5.5 this morning, which is acceptable. We’ll check again tomorrow. For now, focus on resting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, Doctor. I’ll do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You did well yesterday. The angiogram showed some blockages in the arteries of your right leg, but nothing we can’t manage. You’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Does that mean I need another surgery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. The blood flow is sufficient to support healing. We’ll continue monitoring and optimize your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. My foot feels okay, just a little stiff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s normal. Keep it elevated when you can, and we’ll get you walking with support later today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We just got your lab results. Your potassium went up to 6.5 this morning. That’s a bit high, so we’re sending you for a short dialysis session.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? What caused that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not sure. It could be from your meds or diet. As a precaution, we’re stopping your lisinopril and increasing your amlodipine. Nephrology recommended it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was on lisinopril for years. Is it safe to stop?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in your case, it can raise potassium. Amlodipine is safer for now. We’ll keep an eye on your blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I trust you. How long will dialysis take?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: About two hours, with a low-potassium bath. You should feel fine afterward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well on dialysis. Potassium is back down. You’re making good progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. Can I go home tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. If you keep doing this well, we’re planning to discharge you tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What should I do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep your leg elevated, avoid standing too long, and watch for swelling or redness. You can walk, but no heavy lifting for a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my meds? I saw some changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. You’ll stay on amlodipine 5 mg daily instead of 2.5. Metoclopramide is now 5 mg, down from 10. Everything else stays the same.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And the pain pills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get hydrocodone for pain, but only if needed. Don’t take it with Tylenol—there’s already acetaminophen in it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, I remember that from last time. No driving either, I guess.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Wait until you’re off the pain meds. And weigh yourself daily—call if you gain more than three pounds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Any follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll see Dr. Alvarez in vascular surgery next week to check your foot and circulation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re ready to go home. You’ve done really well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Just to confirm—I take the amlodipine, aspirin, diabetes meds, and the pain pills as needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. And keep taking omeprazole, sevelamer with meals, and your insulin. All the others too, except lisinopril.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I can shower?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, gently. Let water run over the groin area, pat dry. No soaking. If there’s drainage, cover it with a bandage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Thank you, Doctor. I’ll take care of myself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call us if you have fever, increased pain, or swelling. Otherwise, see you at your follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. The discharge papers are ready, and a nurse will go over them with you before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’ll wait for her.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—keep protecting your right foot. No barefoot walking, and check it daily for sores.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I learned that the hard way. I’ll be careful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. That’s how we prevent more amputations. You’re doing the right things.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that. I’ll follow all the instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. Have a safe trip home, and we’ll see you soon.
